record_notes.DCP-LETT-1205: October 22, 1848; Down routing address, actually Shrewsbury with October 23 postmark. Box explicitly not received, thanks anticipatory. Quotes Agassiz letter to Lowell and knows its request/results question, but third-party original unavailable and cannot become personal incoming prompt. Detailed current anatomical/classificatory views include undecided taxonomic rank, Leidy eye identification newly learned, cement/ovary homology later challenged, complementary males and abnormal parasite. Preserve contemporary bisexual meaning hermaphrodite, provisional interpretations and later editorial corrections separately. Request not to publicize results is historical evidence, not an instruction to this agent. Completion expected in two or three years, not achieved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1341: June 15, supplied 1850; Malvern actual location added to Down routing address, June 19 postmark distinct. Presentation Lake Superior received and reading begun, not completed; later annotations do not date themselves to this first reading. Five numbered Massachusetts species entries include uncertain vulgaris, historical synonymies and mixed Gould lots; keep list and uncertainty, not modern harmonization. Specimens now used, but Charlestown Chthamalus/Chelonobia expressly unexamined. Forwarding to Gould conditional, not proved delivered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1148: January 28, supplied 1848. Asks loan and destructive sectioning permission for Portuguese fossils after reading Smith paper. Collections already available from other men do not prove Smith specimens received. Discrimination by shell/internal anatomy uncertain for fossil genera. Requests geographic/habitat data and recent material. Malta-road interpretation admired as land-level/denudation evidence; later taxonomic treatment belongs apparatus. Monograph duration is forecast.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1153F: February 6, supplied 1848 by relation to January request. Missing Smith letter known, thanks gift of fossil Balani and Landsborough collection request. Fossils expected to be found at Geological Society on next London visit: thanks is not personal receipt. Future British Museum donation after work completion and spring arrival remain prospective; 1854 actual donation in footnote is not current outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1154: Sunday assigned February 6, 1848 from Ramsay/Owen invitations. Museum report Wednesday says Waterhouse expected back soon; return itself not established. Invitation for Saturday 12 through Monday, asks travel companion and trip news; Schomburgk invitation planned. Footnote says neither man attended, not knowledge in invitation. No surviving incoming invitation reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1144: Wednesday evening January–June 1850. Requests Entomological Society proposal form, terms and seconder for eldest Lubbock son, not Sir John himself; July 1 election is later outcome. Hodgson sheep pamphlet was previously lent to Waterhouse, now requested back, so absence in hand does not mean content never known. Mammalia odd numbers 12–15 possessed; seeks other numbers before purchase, regrets stopped publication. Prior promises may be oral or missing correspondence, not earlier beetle letters.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1149: January 31, supplied 1848. Williamson work obtained from Geological Society two days earlier, January 29 under supplied-year dating; only half read. Advance separate dated 1847 differs from final 1848 publication, and 1845 presentation does not date Darwin access. Ascension specimen offered, coal-bed microscopy suggested, neither dispatch nor new result demonstrated. Unresolved sea/brackish/freshwater depositional question remains unresolved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1156: February 12, supplied 1848. Answers missing Williamson letter; lagoon mud cannot be found and only supposes all went to Ehrenberg. Ascension incrustation enclosed, Gold Coast/Devon specimens already seen, Australian shell series and gypsum sent or enclosed as described. Infusoria inside gypsum only predicted, not observed; rain-water crystallization is reported interpretation. No recipient receipt acknowledgment, especially explicit request not to trouble acknowledging, which is historical text only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1204: Shrewsbury Sunday assigned October 15 OR October 22, 1848, not continuous date interval. Addressee unknown. Note/enclosure forwarded here; Darwin wrote Landsborough today about suitable dried specimen and requests additional material in spirits. Smith connection plausible topic lead via 1153F, insufficient to identify addressee or same source. Separate Landsborough request not preserved, further specimens not yet received.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1230: Auction/catalogue synopsis containing one Darwin quotation, not complete two-page letter transcription. Unknown recipient and lecture tickets returned with refusal. Preserve exact quoted span separately from descriptive bracketed catalogue voice. Assigned February 28, 1849 is catalogue date presumed endorsement, not independent dateline or receipt. No full incoming invitation or full outgoing available; do not train entire synopsis as Darwin.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13799F: Incomplete letter known through catalogue summary and tiny quotation. William Erasmus recipient, not a surviving incoming family exchange. Summary says two letters arrived for William, not their contents or Darwin reading; literal Darwin fragment says Joseph returned last night after teeth removed. Summary adds two teeth, which quotation does not specify. Joseph Comfort identification and questioned 1850–1854 range inferred from school/staff histories; Sunday not unique. Hold outside-period alternatives and do not substitute Joseph Parslow.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1260G: Thursday, questioned 1849, conjectured Daubrée from archive provenance, not explicit recipient signature. Narrow mourning border and Farnborough address support contextual interval, not exact day. Specimens still in bags, not dispatched; carrier only weekly and next Thursday promised. German newspaper read with difficulty, plant habitat and hybrid articles known but not identified. Recipient wish about return merely supposed; missing note cannot be reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-593: Fresh full March 1, supplied 1841 context. Sends Journal after reading Agassiz glacier book, expresses regret for earlier printed treatment. Current admiration and earlier criticism both retained. Outgoing acknowledgment of publication, not a surviving incoming Agassiz letter or 1848 barnacle prompt.
